description: The report-validation sample. Selected against the axes in sample-frame.md, pinned to exact commits resolved 2026-08-12 before any repository was cloned. Not the calibration corpus: no repository here appears in tools/calibration/corpus.json.

repos.name: click
repos.why: Python with the full tool set available - complexipy, radon, ruff, vulture, mypy, pydocstyle, interrogate all apply. The best case, included so the worst cases have something to be compared against.

repos.name: requests
repos.why: A second Python repository, deliberately: one is an anecdote.

repos.name: date-fns
repos.why: TypeScript, thousands of small single-purpose functions. Exercises the declaration population at a shape Python repositories do not produce.

repos.name: formik
repos.why: TypeScript with visibly reduced maintenance activity. The condition axis: a report that only works on actively-tended code is a report for nobody.

repos.name: babel
repos.why: The monorepo case - many packages under one root. Exercises paths, exclusions and whether one score over a hundred packages means anything.

repos.name: gson
repos.why: Java, where only lizard and jscpd apply of the installed pool. Coverage must say so rather than scoring the gap as clean.

repos.name: cobra
repos.why: Go: same partial-coverage case as Java, different language, to separate 'the Java adapter is broken' from 'non-Python coverage is thin'.

repos.name: ripgrep
repos.why: Rust, actively maintained, large. lizard supports it; nothing else installed does.

repos.name: kilo
repos.why: A text editor in roughly a thousand lines of C, one source file, untouched for years. Two axes at once: far below the population floor, and visibly unmaintained. The report must withhold the score and name the shortfall - this is the hello-world A+ case, in the wild.

repos.name: curl
repos.why: Large C, thirty years old, actively maintained, famously careful about quality. If the tool calls this bad code, the tool is wrong.

repos.name: json
repos.why: Header-only C++, where a single file legitimately runs to tens of thousands of lines. Exercises whether the file-size dimension can distinguish a convention from a defect.

repos.name: whisper.cpp
repos.why: C++ with vendored dependencies in-tree. Exercises whether exclusions keep third-party code out of the user's score - the defect that had vulture reporting 517 findings, all inside .venv.

repos.name: lapack
repos.why: Fortran, and the hardest case in the sample: numerical code whose conventions predate every threshold in the rubric. Included precisely because it is expected to score badly for reasons that are not defects.

repos.name: machinelearning-samples
repos.why: C#, and a tree of many independent sample projects rather than one library. Exercises the case where 'this repository' is not one codebase at all.
